reason: The skin cell needs to copy its DNA before it can divide, and the building blocks are shown arriving at that cell.
expectation: The cell will copy its chromosomes in preparation for division.

effect: The chromosomes are copied into joined sister chromatids, ready for separation.
reaction: The before-and-after description makes the copying step clear.
reason: The separating machinery is positioned to attach to the copied chromosomes.
expectation: The machinery will separate the sister chromatids toward opposite sides of the cell.

effect: The chromosome sets are separated, but the cell still has one shared interior.
reaction: The description clearly distinguishes chromosome separation from cell division.
reason: The division ring can now divide the cell around the two separated chromosome sets.

choice.combine: Skin cell with separated chromosome sets

expectation: The ring will pinch the cell into two daughter cells, each with a chromosome set.

effect: The division ring produced two new skin cells, each with a complete chromosome set.
reaction: The sequence makes the final separation clear.
reason: Erythropoietin is shown carrying a kidney signal to marrow, where the red-cell precursors are.
expectation: The signal will promote the production of new red blood cells.

effect: The kidney signal leads the marrow precursors to develop into red cells; the result also shows low oxygen as the cue.
reaction: The kidney-to-marrow connection is clear, though the cells are still described as developing.
reason: The new skin cells appear ready to be connected to the body whose skin they renew.
expectation: The body will gain a renewing skin layer.

effect: The new cells are now connected to the body's renewing skin, with shedding shown at the surface.
reaction: The link between cell division and ongoing skin renewal is clear.
reason: The developing red cells appear ready to connect to the same body's blood renewal.
expectation: The body will show developing red cells contributing to blood renewal.

effect: The body now shows skin and blood renewal, and the next goal is to remodel existing bone.
reaction: The kidney-to-marrow link gives blood renewal a useful connection to oxygen supply.
reason: Bone-removing cells and bone-forming cells suggest successive roles in remodeling, so I will check how the removing cells can be used.
expectation: The available partners should show how bone removal begins.

effect: The inspection automatically applied the bone-removing cells to the body, showing old bone being removed.
reaction: The automatic step makes the start of remodeling clear.
reason: Bone-forming cells can rebuild the patch after old bone is removed.
expectation: The cells will form new bone in the remodeling patch.

effect: Bone-forming cells rebuilt the patch, completing the bone-remodeling goal and the chapter.
reaction: The final picture ties the renewal processes back to the working body.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following the skin cell from copied chromosomes to two daughter cells made the stages of division clear and connected them to skin renewal.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the finished skin and red cells to the body was straightforward, but those actions offered less new information than making the cells.

surprise.text: The red-cell result added a useful connection: low oxygen prompts a kidney signal that reaches the marrow.

arbitrary.text: The bone-removing cells had an obvious role, but I was unsure how to start the construction until inspection revealed their partner and automatically combined them.

continue.text: I would be interested in another chapter if it explored a new relationship as clearly as the kidney-to-marrow signal. The assembly steps were sometimes predictable, but the connections between organs gave them purpose.
